It is recommended, in the dofe of a few drops, in nervous and hyfteric complaints. Boerhaave holds it in great eftem againt epilepties, and fupprefions of the uterine purgations, occationed by weaknefs and inactivity.<x_0.9746><y_0.1117><class_Text>

<x_0.3301><y_0.1125>_535._ _Effential oil of rue-leaves_. L.<x_0.8418><y_0.1313><class_Section-header>

<x_0.21><y_0.1266>The oil of rue has a very acid tafte, and a pene- trating fmell, refembling that of the herb, but rather more unpleasant. It is fometimes made ufe of in hy- fteric diforders, and as an anthelmintic ; as alfo in epilepties proceeding from a relaxed flate of the nerves.<x_0.9756><y_0.2133><class_Text>

<x_0.2109><y_0.2117>Rue yields its oil very faringly. The largeft quantity is obtained from it when the flowers are ready to fall off, and the feeds begin to flow themfelves: fuitable maceration, previous to the diftillation, is here extremely necelitary.<x_0.9766><y_0.2859><class_Text>

<x_0.3066><y_0.2875>_536._ _Effential oil of favin leaves_. L. E.<x_0.8857><y_0.3063><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2139><y_0.3031>This oil is a celebrated uterine and emmenagogue ; in cold phlegmatic habits, it is undoubtedly a medicine of good service, though not capable of performing what it has been ufually reprefented to do. The dofe is, two or three drops or more.<x_0.9795><y_0.3766><class_Text>

<x_0.3291><y_0.3789>_537._ _Effential oil of faffafras_. L. E.<x_0.8623><y_0.3969><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2158><y_0.3937>This is the moft ponderosus of all the known effen- zial oils, but rifles in diftillation with sufficient eafe: it appears limpid as water, has a moderately pungent tafte, a very fragrant fmell, exactly refembling that of the faffafras. It stands greatly commended as a fudo- rifc, and for purifying the blood and juices: it is like- wife fuppofed to be of fervice in humoural athmas and coughs. The dofe is from one drop to eight or ten ; though Geoffroy goes as far as 20.<x_0.9824><y_0.5227><class_Text>

<x_0.2227><y_0.5219>The decoction remaining after the diftillation of the oil, affords, by infipiffation, an uful extract, of a mild, bitterifh, fubaftringent tafte. Hoffman fays, he has given it with great benefit, in dofes of a feruple, as a corroborant in cachectic cafes, in the decline of intermitting fevers, and for abating hypochondriacal fpafms.<x_0.9902><y_0.6234><class_Text>

<x_0.3877><y_0.625>_538._ _Oil of turpentine_. L. E.<x_0.8281><y_0.643><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2256><y_0.6398>This is distilled in the fame manner as the foregoing oils, and is strictly an effectual one, though not ufually ranked in this clafs: it is commonly, but improperly, called _fpirit of turpentine_. It is employed in large quantities for fome mechanic purposes, and hence the diftillation of it is become a particular buti- nefs.<x_0.9912><y_0.7398><class_Text>

<x_0.2266><y_0.7383>This oil is a very hot, filmulating medicine. It is fometimes given as a fudorific and diuretic, in the dofe of two or three drops: in larger dofes, it is apt to greatly heat the body, occasion pain of the head, an effusion of the femen and liquor of the proflate glands. It has neverthelefs been of late taken in confiderable dofes (along with honey or other convenient vehicles) against the feiatica ; and, as is laid, with good fuccefs. Some have recommended it againt venceal runnings: but here it has produced mif- chievous consequences, inflaming the parts and ag- grasating the diforder.
